title: Plastic Alternatives
desc: Understand materials that can replace single-use plastic, how to test them honestly, and how to plan a small product switch.
outcomes: Explain plastic types and the problem of waste.
Test an alternative for use and cost.
Judge claims such as biodegradable and compostable.
Plan a product switch for a small business.
task: Choose one single-use plastic item, test two alternatives, compare cost and impact, and write a switch plan with customer message.
condition: Samples of items, a scale and basic tools, a spreadsheet, two peers and a mentor. Safe, non-food-contact tests unless approved.
standard: Tests are repeatable; claims are checked against recognised definitions; cost per use is shown; end-of-life route exists locally; peers rate Meets or better.
who: Shop owners, packaging buyers, students, municipal staff.
evidence: test sheet, comparison table, switch plan

Reduce, reuse, recycle. (Covered in module 1: The waste problem. To pass that module: List with counts.)

They enter food and water. (Covered in module 2: Types of plastic and codes. To pass that module: At least 9 correct.)
Compostable equals biodegradable?
No. (Covered in module 3: Alternatives. To pass that module: Pros and cons.)

Strength, leak, heat or shelf life. (Covered in module 4: Testing. To pass that module: Table complete.)

Material, making, transport, use, end of life. (Covered in module 5: Life-cycle thinking. To pass that module: Method stated.)

Reuse items spread cost. (Covered in module 6: Claims and labels. To pass that module: Claims checked.)

Reduce. (Covered in module 8: Switch plan. To pass that module: Measures are clear.)

ladder: The waste problem

L1: learner can name plastic problems. Focus module: The waste problem (Understand, 3 h). Why plastic matters. Key points: Single-use items are used for minutes and last for centuries. Microplastics enter food and water. Reduce first, reuse second, recycle third.

Teach: open with the worked example. Refill stations cut bottle use more than any new material. Then set the activity: Audit the plastic you use in a week. Mark against the standard: List with counts. Check at this level: Order of waste actions? Model answer: Reduce, reuse, recycle. Audit.
Types of plastic and codes

L2: learner knows reduce-reuse-recycle. Focus module: Types of plastic and codes (Understand, 3 h). Know what you hold. Key points: Resin codes 1 to 7. Some types are widely recycled, some not. Mixed and dirty plastic is hard to recycle.

Teach: open with the worked example. PET bottles are often recycled; film is not. Then set the activity: Sort 10 items. Mark against the standard: At least 9 correct. Check at this level: Why microplastics matter? Model answer: They enter food and water. Rule.
Alternatives

L3: learner can test options. Focus module: Alternatives (Understand, 4 h). Many options. Key points: Paper, glass, metal, plant fibres, starch-based, compostable blends. Each has a cost and an impact. Reuse systems often win.

Teach: open with the worked example. A cafe moves to returnable cups. Then set the activity: Make an options table. Mark against the standard: Pros and cons. Check at this level: Compostable equals biodegradable? Model answer: No. Test.
Testing
L4: learner can compare life cycles. Focus module: Testing (Apply, 4 h). Do real tests. Key points: Strength, leak, heat, shelf life, cost per use. Repeat three times. Record failures.

Teach: open with the worked example. A starch bag tears at 3 kg; paper holds 5 kg. Then set the activity: Test two options. Mark against the standard: Table complete. Check at this level: Name a test. Model answer: Strength, leak, heat or shelf life. Compare.
Life-cycle thinking

L5: learner can review claims. Focus module: Life-cycle thinking (Analyse, 4 h). Look at the whole life. Key points: Raw material, making, transport, use, end of life. Reuse items win after enough uses. Local conditions change results.

Teach: open with the worked example. A glass jar needs 12 uses to beat plastic. Then set the activity: Do a simple comparison. Mark against the standard: Method stated. Check at this level: Life-cycle stages? Model answer: Material, making, transport, use, end of life. Claims.
Customers and cost
L6: learner can lead a switch. Focus module: Customers and cost (Evaluate, 3 h). Make the switch fair. Key points: Cost per use, not per piece. Deposit or discount schemes. Explain simply.

Teach: open with the worked example. A refill discount repays within 20 uses. Then set the activity: Cost your switch. Mark against the standard: Currency shown. Check at this level: Why cost per use? Model answer: Reuse items spread cost. Plan.
Switch plan
L7: learner can audit. Focus module: Switch plan (Create, 3 h). Plan and review. Key points: Steps, dates, owners, measures. Pilot in one store. Report results.

Teach: open with the worked example. Plastic bags fall by 70% in a month. Then set the activity: Present the plan. Mark against the standard: Measures are clear. Check at this level: Name a label risk. Model answer: Greenwashing. Peer audit.
